title: The last-minute luxury bargain mostly isn't
subtitle: Waiting works on a 4,000-berth ship. It rarely works on a 300-guest one.

text: Small ships run out of cabins before they run out of price.
sub: A line with a few hundred suites has no distressed inventory to dump. It has a waitlist. Scarcity is the pricing strategy.

points.label: Season opens
points.value: Full choice of suite category, deck and dining. Fares calm and stable.

points.label: Wave months
points.value: The heaviest promotion calendar of the year. Credit and perks are richest.

points.label: Mid-cycle
points.value: Best cabins thinning. Fares firm as the sailing fills out.

points.label: Final payment
points.value: The real cliff edge. After it, changes cost money and choice narrows.

points.label: Last weeks
points.value: What's left is what nobody chose. Occasionally a gift, usually a compromise.

title: Three cases where waiting costs you

items.head: You want a specific suite
items.body: Aft, midship, or a particular category on a small ship. There are only ever a handful, and they go first.

items.head: The dates are fixed
items.body: School terms, an anniversary, a Greek islands sailing in shoulder season. No flexibility means no leverage.

items.head: Air is part of the plan
items.body: The cruise may soften. The flights almost never do, and they are the half nobody watches.

quote: Booking early buys you choice. Booking late buys you what's left. Only one of those is a saving.

text: Book early, then keep the booking under review.
sub: Early gets you the cabin. A watched booking gets you the fare - if it drops before final payment it can often be rebooked. That only works if someone is looking.

title: Save this before your next booking
body: Or tell me the season you have in mind and I'll send back the shoulder-season calendar for it.
